name: Faith
label: Dischord
lede: Faith lasted about two years and left one side of a split LP and an eight-song EP, and a lot of D.C. kids felt closer to them than to Minor Threat.

eras.title: The scene goes quiet, Faith fills it
eras.text: By fall 1981 several D.C. bands had broken up at once, Minor Threat briefly among them, and the scene went quiet. SOA veterans Michael Hampton and Ivor Hanson, Untouchables singer Alec MacKaye and Wilson High bassist Chris Bald formed Faith, and within weeks of their first show they were opening for Bad Brains at CBGB.

years.h: Faith forms out of SOA and the Untouchables
years.p: Michael Hampton and Ivor Hanson come over from [[SOA|e54cb250-3502-4c32-9482-70488bd9a8cb]], Alec MacKaye from the Untouchables, and fellow Wilson High kid Chris Bald picks up the bass. Alec is [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]]'s younger brother.

years.cap: Faith at the Chancery, Washington, D.C., around 1981-82: Chris Bald, Alec MacKaye, Michael Hampton, with Ivor Hanson on drums.
years.h: Faith's first show is at H.B. Woodlawn High School
years.p: The Arlington high school gym hosts the debut. Before the year is out they're also playing the Chancery in D.C.

years.cap: Recorded at CBGB, December 1981, and released later by Outer Battery.
years.h: A few weeks in, Faith open for Bad Brains at CBGB
years.p: Faith are in New York opening for [[Bad Brains|e919b253-da5b-4aae-a444-6a368376a2d6]]. Someone rolls tape, and the set later comes out as Live at CBGB's on Outer Battery.
years.xp: The CBGB set is the band's only live record. It was taped in December 1981, the month Faith also cut their 11-song demo with Ian MacKaye at Inner Ear, and it came out long after the band had ended.

eras.title: Their side of the record
eras.text: Dischord paired Faith with Void for the split LP Faith/Void, and the band played the Wilson Center and Woodlawn High School while its sound started to change.

yt: Full set at the Wilson Center, 1982
years.h: Faith/Void, Dischord No. 8, Faith on one side
years.p: Twelve Faith songs, with [[Void|960a1d2f-2b5f-4fcf-bf11-4957529a6508]] on the other side, recorded at Inner Ear. The sleeve credits production to Ian, Jeff, Don, Bert and the band.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia, the first pressing sold out in two weeks. The Washington Post later described Faith as taking the snarl of British punk, speeding it up and making it distinctly American. Next to Void's chaotic side, the Faith side is taut and pointed.

The record found fans far from D.C. Wikipedia credits Kurt Cobain with putting Faith/Void in his top 50 albums of all time, and Thurston Moore with calling it the most potent distillation of early D.C. straight edge hardcore.

years.h: Live at the Wilson Center, April 4, 1982
yt: Live at the Wilson Center, April 4, 1982

eras.title: Stopping at the top
eras.text: Eddie Janney made Faith a five-piece in early 1983 and the songs got longer. By August the band was done, and its last record came out after its last show, which is part of why it hit people so hard.

yt: Live at Space II Arcade, July 20, 1983
years.h: Eddie Janney joins Faith on second guitar
years.p: Alec MacKaye's old Untouchables bandmate [[Eddie Janney|323dd1dd-23e4-45ce-9aa9-c5492096d604]] joins Michael Hampton on guitar, and Faith become a five-piece.
years.xp: Dischord dates Janney's arrival to early 1983. Wikipedia and Washington City Paper put it at the end of 1982. Either way, the five-piece lineup is the one caught in this July 1983 set at Space II Arcade in D.C., a month before the last show.

years.big: "It was a good time to stop."
years.h: Faith play their last show as headliners
years.p: Michael Hampton's verdict, decades later, on the August 17, 1983 show that ended Faith about two years after their November 1981 debut.
years.xp:
No single reason for the split is on the record. Hampton, looking back, simply thought the timing was right.

The audience felt otherwise. Dischord's own bio says that while Minor Threat gets held up as the defining D.C. band of those years, for many people who lived there it was Faith they felt closest to, and that it was a sad day when they played their last show.

years.h: Subject to Change, Dischord No. 11, arrives after the breakup
years.p: Eight songs, about thirteen minutes, produced by Ian MacKaye and Faith at Inner Ear. It comes out roughly four months after the last show, so most listeners meet the five-piece Faith after it's gone.
years.xp:
Subject to Change is the only record of the five-piece Faith, with Janney's guitar alongside Hampton's.

The fans who missed that lineup live took the record hard. Ian MacKaye summed up the reaction years later: "People just loved that band."

eras.title: Everybody starts the next band
eras.text: Follow almost any branch of mid-80s Dischord back far enough and you hit one of Faith's five members.

years.h: Janney co-founds [[Rites of Spring|b2ff1a6d-9198-4646-b068-8965242d245b]] with Guy Picciotto
years.p: The former Faith guitarist starts the band with [[Guy Picciotto|f8200cea-b5e9-4145-b5a5-1d0838f2c288]], part of the wave that follows hardcore in D.C.

years.h: Three of Faith back Ian MacKaye in [[Embrace|9d1ad8e3-8740-429a-bdc5-52f96a9c4431]]
years.p: Hampton, Bald and Hanson play behind Ian, who has moved on from [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]]. The older brother ends up singing in front of his younger brother Alec's old band.

years.h: Janney and Hampton reunite in One Last Wish
years.p: The two Faith guitarists form [[One Last Wish|94f18045-7fe2-41df-bf24-0bed21c88eb8]], which later becomes [[Happy Go Licky|4c18be5e-2e53-41a4-a4a1-d9080ff88f8c]]. Alec MacKaye and Bald go on to form [[Ignition|3cb2b7d6-1f0b-4ac5-b67f-52132f3d3b61]].

years.h: Drummer and guitarist from SOA, Faith and Embrace try again, as Manifesto
years.p: Hampton and Hanson, who played together in SOA, Faith and Embrace, team up once more in Manifesto, ten years after SOA.

eras.title: Back to the tapes
eras.text: Nearly thirty years on, Dischord went back to Faith's tapes. The 2011 reissue Subject to Change plus First Demo put the band's first recordings next to its last and sent a new round of writers back to Faith/Void.

yt: Live at the Wilson Center, June 25, 1982
years.h: Faith are on Dischord's 20th-anniversary box set
years.p: Faith take their place on 20 Years of Dischord, which includes a clip of the band live at the Wilson Center.

years.h: Faith's 1981 demo comes out after 30 years on the shelf
years.p: The eleven-song December 1981 demo, produced by Ian MacKaye at Inner Ear, is paired with a remastered Subject to Change as Dischord No. 172.
years.xp:
Nearly every song on the demo had been re-recorded for Faith/Void in 1982, so the tape sat on the shelf.

The 2011 edition was remastered from the original tapes and was the EP's first time on vinyl since 1988, this time on clear vinyl.
play: Subject to Change plus First Demo

years.h: Craig Finn tells The Guardian that Faith/Void is vital
years.p: [[The Hold Steady|4883523d-fc0e-4d0d-802c-91379e767083]]'s Craig Finn calls the 1982 split LP one of the most vital hardcore records ever released.
